subject: Subprocessor addition notice — TechSupply / Request for DPA evidence & redlines

Cc: legal@techsupply.io
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Notice: adding CloudRelay as subprocessor (summary + attachments)

Hi Nikhil,

Following our contract terms (section 8.2), TechSupply is notifying Redwood Inference that we intend to engage CloudRelay Ltd. as a subcontractor for log aggregation and edge routing for the Redwood integration. The change is limited to telemetry and log streaming; no inference model hosting.

Summary: 
- Subprocessor: CloudRelay Ltd. (UK)
- Purpose: encrypted log forwarding and ephemeral storage for debug traces
- Data types: service-level logs, request/response metadata (no raw customer prompts)
- Proposed effective date: 2027-01-12

Attached: TechSupply_subprocessor_notice.pdf (list + short SoW). We also attached our proposed DPA redline that adds CloudRelay as an approved subprocessor. Please confirm whether Redwood requires additional evidence (SOC2, encryption at rest keys, data residency guarantees) and whether Redwood will require an amendment to the Order Form for this change.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Head of Partnerships
TechSupply Solutions

Thanks for the ping, Nikhil. I reviewed TechSupply's draft DPA redline. High-level notes: 

1) Required language additions
- Insert explicit limitation: CloudRelay may only process telemetry/logs and is prohibited from using any aggregated telemetry to train models or infer customer data.
- Add a dedicated subprocessor annex referencing the exact SoW and list of endpoints CloudRelay will access.
- Preserve our right to audit (30 days notice) and require remediation plan within 14 days for any control gaps.

2) Data residency and cross-border transfers
- Their redline lacks clarity on data residency. If CloudRelay stores logs in EU for EU customers, we need an export/control clause. Request SCCs or equivalent if EU data involved.

3) Indemnity / liability cap carveouts
- Ask for an explicit liability carveout for security incidents caused by CloudRelay where TechSupply failed to enforce the subproc terms.

4) Evidence set we need before consent
- SOC 2 Type II report (last 12 months)
- Network architecture diagram showing separation of PII and telemetry
- KMS details (who controls keys and whether Redwood can require CMEK for private deployments)

I attached a short redline snippet that replaces TechSupply's permissive language with our standard flowdown text. See attachment: TechSupply_DPA_redline.docx.

If Marissa signs off on the evidence set, I'll prepare a clean redline to send to TechSupply with track changes and a short list of non-negotiables. We should also flag to SalesOps that this may require an Order Form amendment for customers who require dedicated private deployments.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Notice: adding CloudRelay as subprocessor (need intake + redline triage)

Looping in a couple of operational checks from Security/Trust: 

- KV/Cache exposure: confirm whether CloudRelay's pipeline includes any short-lived KV caches that could capture requests. If so we need a hard prohibition on storing customer prompts or PII even transiently.
- Retention windows: ask for retention policy for logs (default 30 days for debug, longer only with customer consent).
- Private deployment customers: if TechSupply serves our Private customers (on-prem or VPC), we must require that CloudRelay operate entirely within the customer's environment or that we pre-approve any cross-border movement.
- Incident response: include an SLA for notification (24 hrs) and mandatory cooperation for forensic analysis.

I'll be comfortable with a consent if TechSupply produces SOC2 Type II, the network diagram, and confirms retention policy <= 30 days for general logs. If CloudRelay refuses any of the controls above, suggest escalation to Legal Ops and an opt-out for impacted customers.

Marissa Cole
Trust & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Lydia — thanks for the notice and for the draft redline. Per our internal review (cc'd Kimberly and Marissa), Redwood can provisionally accept CloudRelay for telemetry-only processing subject to the following deliverables before we issue formal consent: 

1) Evidence pack (deliver by 2026-12-16):
  - SOC 2 Type II (latest 12 months) for CloudRelay
  - Network architecture diagram that shows segmentation between telemetry and any PII stores
  - KMS and key custody statement (who holds keys; support for customer CMEK if required)
  - Retention policy for logs (<= 30 days for general logs; any longer retention must be tied to explicit customer consent)

2) Contractual changes (please return by 2026-12-16):
  - Replace permissive subprocessing clause with our standard flowdown language (we attached suggested redline).
  - Add express prohibition on using telemetry to train models or build profiling products.
  - Include audit right (30 days notice) and remediation requirement (14 days).
  - Liability carveout: TechSupply must require CloudRelay to be contractually bound to indemnify Redwood for security incidents arising from their failure to comply with the flowdown.

3) Order Form / Commercial:
  - If CloudRelay will touch any customer marked as a Private deployment or with EU residency constraints, we will require an Order Form amendment that enumerates permitted subprocessors and residency guarantees. Please flag impacted customers and share a proposed orderform_amendment_stub.pdf for review.

We can schedule a 30-min call next week to walk through the items; otherwise please send the evidence and an updated redline and we'll route for final sign-off.
